samples.summary: Wiring `requestLayoutRefresh = recomputeLayout` defeats the incremental layout cache: every keystroke now ends in a full-document relayout
samples.evidence:
`recomputeLayout` (editor.ts:1522-1534) passes `dirtyBlockIds` to `computeLayout` and then unconditionally sets `dirtyBlockIds = undefined`. `computeLayout` (view/layout.ts:456-459) only reuses the cache when `dirtyBlockIds != null` (`canUseCache = cache != null && dirtyBlockIds != null && ...`).

With the new render-hold, an ordinary keystroke runs: `handleInput` -> `withUndoUnit` -> `markDirty(blockId)` -> `this.requestRender()` which, because `undoUnitDepth > 0`, calls `requestLayoutRefresh()` = `recomputeLayout()`. That pass consumes `dirtyBlockIds` (incremental, correct) and resets it to `undefined`. The unit then exits and `withUndoUnit`'s finally replays `this.requestRender()` -> `hostRequestRender` -> `renderWithScroll` -> `render()` -> `recomputeLayout()` again, this time with `dirtyBlockIds === undefined`, so `canUseCache` is false and the whole document is re-measured from scratch before the paint.

So the layout that actually gets painted is a full O(all blocks) re-measure on *every* keystroke, plus the incremental pass that preceded it. Before this change typing did exactly one incremental pass. The result is still visually correct, but the incremental layout cache — the thing that keeps typing responsive in a long document — is bypassed on the hottest path in the editor.

samples.summary: MemDocStore.batch() now runs on every keystroke and costs 2 full document clones + 3 full-document JSON.stringify per batch
samples.evidence: `batch()` does `cloneDocument(this.doc)` (line 256), `JSON.stringify(beforeClone)` (257), `JSON.stringify(top)` for the adoption check (259), and on exit another `cloneDocument(this.doc)` + `JSON.stringify` (289). `TextEditor.handleInput` now wraps *every* character insert in `withUndoUnit` -> `doc.batch()` (text-editor.ts:1020), including the common no-selection case that previously opened no batch at all. Combined with `saveSnapshot()`'s own `cloneDocument`, a single keypress in any MemDocStore host (slides text boxes, the docs demo app, the visual harness) now serialises the entire document ~4 times instead of once.

samples.summary: `willWrite()` is called before the lookup that can throw, so a mutator that fails without writing still destroys the redo stack
samples.evidence: `updateBlock` (77), `deleteBlock` (101), `insertBlockAfter` (88), `insertText` (350), `deleteText` (357), `applyStyle` (362), `splitBlock` (376), `setBlockType` (398), `applyBlockStyle` (430), the table mutators (305, 311, 317, 325, 335, 341) and `insertImageInline` (471) all call `this.willWrite()` *before* `findBlockInAnyArray`/`findBlock`, which throws `Block not found: <id>` for an id that is not in the document (a routine outcome when a remote peer deleted the block). The redo stack is cleared even though the call wrote nothing and threw. `deleteBlockByIndex` (107-111) shows the other ordering — bounds check first, then `willWrite()` — so the two are inconsistent. The doc comment only justifies clearing before a *partial* write, not before a lookup failure.

samples.summary: Software-Hangul commit opens an undo unit without the `saveSnapshot()` the new contract requires, so undo restores the post-edit caret
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s own doc comment (text-editor.ts:3828-3832) states "`saveSnapshot()` must be called before opening a unit, never inside one" because on `YorkieDocStore` it is what stages the pre-edit caret (`setCursorForHistory` -> `pendingCursorPos`, consumed by the first write inside the update via `recordHistoryPresence`). The new unit at 5891-5894 (`deleteSelection()` + `docInsertText`) has no `saveSnapshot()` anywhere above it on this path: `handleInput` returns at line 1008 before reaching its `saveSnapshot()` at 1014, and the `saveSnapshot()` at 5905 only runs in the `result.composing && !result.commit` branch. So `consumePendingCursor()` returns null for this change and Yorkie records no reverse presence — undo of a jamo typed over a selection leaves the caret at the post-edit position. (The pre-existing code had the same gap, but the change turns these two writes into one unit and documents the invariant this site violates.)

samples.summary: Callers that call `deleteSelection()` then `requestRender()` now paint twice
samples.evidence: `deleteSelection()` opens its own `withUndoUnit`, whose finally replays the held interior `requestRender()` as a full host render. `handleCut` at 1465-1467 and 1475-1477 then immediately call `this.requestRender()` again, and `applyHangulResult` does the same at 5920 after its unit at 5891. Each redundant call is a full-document `recomputeLayout` + `paint` (see the `dirtyBlockIds` finding). Not visible to the user — both happen in the same task — but it doubles the cost on cut and on every software-Hangul syllable.

samples.summary: `pastePlainTextFromClipboard`'s bare `catch {}` also swallows failures of the store writes it now wraps
samples.evidence: The `try` at 4244 spans the clipboard read *and* the whole `withUndoUnit` write body (4255-4261). Its comment says "Clipboard API unavailable or permission denied — silently ignore", but any throw out of `deleteSelection()`, `insertPlainText()` or the store's `batch()` is discarded on the same channel. On `YorkieDocStore` the batch rolls the update back, so the user sees a plain-text paste do nothing at all with no error reported anywhere; on `MemDocStore` partial writes stand. The change moved these writes into a unit without narrowing the `try` to the `await`.

verdict.reason: Every claimed location is accurate. recomputeLayout (editor.ts:1522-1534) passes dirtyBlockIds to computeLayout then clears it to undefined; computeLayout only reuses the cache when dirtyBlockIds != null (layout.ts:456-459, reuse branch at 535, otherwise full layoutBlock at 538). The render-hold wrapper (text-editor.ts:734-743) calls requestLayoutRefresh() — wired to recomputeLayout at editor.ts:2531 — while undoUnitDepth > 0, consuming and clearing the dirty set; withUndoUnit's finally (text-editor.ts:3846-3848) then replays requestRender() → hostRequestRender = renderWithScroll (editor.ts:2473) → render() → recomputeLayout() (editor.ts:2208-2211) with dirtyBlockIds now undefined, so canUseCache is false and the whole document is re-measured. The ordinary typing path matches: markDirty (text-editor.ts:1035) precedes requestRender (1047) inside the unit, and nothing re-populates the dirty set between the two passes (markDirty defined editor.ts:1582-1587). So the painted layout is a full O(all blocks) re-measure on every keystroke plus a preceding incremental pass — a broken cache invariant on the editor's hottest path. I found no guard, no alternate path, and no factual error to refute on.
